culture.name: Peru
culture.language: Spanish, Quechua or your home language
culture.timeDifference: It is about the same time there, give or take an hour.
culture.homeTravelNote: a flight of most of a day, far enough that a visit home takes planning

cookLines: Strips of beef hit the hot pan with red onion and tomato, and the whole apartment smells like home.
You taste the lomo saltado and add a splash more soy sauce and vinegar, the way your father would.
{roommate} wanders in and asks what smells so good.
You share plates at the counter, rice on one side and fries on the other, and for an hour the world is small and warm.

festivals.title: The purple month
festivals.body: October at home is the month of the Señor de los Milagros, with purple habits, long processions through Lima and turrón de Doña Pepa in every bakery. Here it is midterm season.
festivals.join: Join the procession at the Peruvian parish in the city.
festivals.joinText: The brotherhood carries the image slowly down a street you have never seen, and the hymns are the ones you grew up with. Afterward there are anticuchos and picarones in the church hall.
festivals.host: Bake turrón de Doña Pepa and share it.
festivals.hostText: The anise dough and the sticky syrup take all afternoon. Your friends pick off the sprinkles first, exactly as you did as a child.
festivals.skip: Wear something purple and call home.
festivals.skipText: Your grandmother notices the purple at once. She tells you about the procession, street by street.

festivals.title: Nochebuena
festivals.body: At home Christmas Eve means waiting until midnight, panetón with hot chocolate, a nativity scene and the whole family in one room. Here the dorms are emptying out for the break.
festivals.join: Go to a Peruvian family's Christmas Eve dinner.
festivals.joinText: At midnight everyone hugs everyone, and someone hands you a slice of panetón and a mug of hot chocolate. You stay until the small hours.
festivals.host: Host a midnight hot chocolate for whoever is still on campus.
festivals.hostText: You find panetón at the Latin American grocery store and make the chocolate thick, with cinnamon and cloves. Six people toast at midnight with paper cups.
festivals.skip: Video-call the family dinner and go to bed early.
festivals.skipText: Your little cousins pass the phone around the table. You fall asleep to the sound of home.

festivals.title: Fiestas Patrias, 28 July
festivals.body: At home red and white flags hang from every house, there are parades and two days of holiday for Independence Day. Here it is a quiet summer weekday.
festivals.join: Go to the Peruvian festival in the city.
festivals.joinText: There is a marinera on stage, a cajón keeping time and a long line for ceviche and anticuchos. You run into someone from your own district.
festivals.host: Cook for friends and put a small flag on the table.
festivals.hostText: Your friends try ají de gallina and ask for the recipe. You toast with chicha morada and teach them to say "¡Viva el Perú!"
festivals.skip: Send greetings to the family group chat and carry on.
festivals.skipText: Your phone fills with red and white. You smile at every message on your way to work.

familyCall: Lima is on almost the same clock as the East Coast, so your mother calls just after lunch on Sunday.
She asks if you are eating well and whether you have found good ají yet.
Your father asks about your classes, and your grandmother takes the phone to ask when you are coming home.
You hang up hungry and homesick, and a little lighter.
culture.homeMoneyNote: Money from home is converted from soles, and every move in the exchange rate shows up in your account.
culture.familySupportNote: Designed value, kept at the India baseline of 1.0. The research has no sourced figure that would justify more or less family support for Peruvian students. The cost of flights home is handled by roundTripFlightUsd, not by this factor.

entryNotes.F1: About 5,667 Peruvians studied in the US in 2024/25, a record and the 25th largest group; Peruvian nationals received 2,519 F-1 visas in FY2024.
entryNotes.H1B: Peruvian nationals received 336 H-1B visas in FY2024, and Peruvians wait in the shorter Rest of World green card queue, not India's or China's.
entryNotes.B2: Peru is not in the Visa Waiver Program, so Peruvians cannot use ESTA and need a visitor visa before any trip.
entryNotes.O1: Peruvian nationals received 93 O-1 visas in FY2024, up from 27 in FY2018.
entryNotes.FAM: Peru is charged to the Rest of World queue and, unlike Brazil, Colombia and Venezuela, was eligible for the DV-2026 Diversity Visa lottery.
entryNotes.EWI: Border Patrol encounters of Peruvians at the southwest border fell from 74,665 in FY2023 to 427 in FY2026, and entering without inspection usually blocks a green card from inside the US later.
entryNotes.ASY: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 611 and denied 2,424 asylum cases from Peruvian nationals, about 20 percent of decisions.

facts.title: Time difference to Lima
facts.text: Lima is on UTC-5 all year with no daylight saving time. It is level with US Eastern in winter and 1 hour behind in summer, and 3 hours ahead of Pacific in winter and 2 in summer.

facts.title: Round-trip flight, Peru to US
facts.text: Design estimate of $750. No sourced fare range for Peru to US round trips was found in the research; real fares vary widely by route and season.

facts.title: F-1 visas issued to Peruvians
facts.text: Peruvian nationals received 2,519 F-1 visas in FY2024, close to the 2,653 of FY2022, and 2,087 in FY2025. Figures are State Department data republished by VisaGrader.

facts.title: Peruvian students in the US
facts.text: Open Doors counted 5,667 Peruvian students in US higher education in 2024/25, up from 5,505 the year before, the 25th largest group.

facts.title: Remittances to Peru
facts.text: Peru received $5.368 billion in remittances in 2025, about $434 million more than in 2024, with the United States the main source (Central Reserve Bank of Peru, as reported by Andina).

facts.title: H-1B visas for Peruvians
facts.text: Peruvian nationals received 336 H-1B visas in FY2024 and 356 in FY2025, up from 213 in FY2018. Peru's share of all H-1B approvals was not found; many people switch status inside the US without a visa stamp.

facts.title: Asylum decisions for Peruvian applicants
facts.text: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 611 and denied 2,424 asylum cases from Peruvian nationals, about 20 percent of decisions. Another 1,562 were not adjudicated. Individual claims matter more than averages.

facts.title: Family green card queue for Peru
facts.text: Peru is charged to the Rest of World queue, with no separate column in the Visa Bulletin. November 2026 final action dates as transcribed by a law firm: adult children of citizens (F1) 22 Jan 2021, married children (F3) 22 Oct 2015, siblings (F4) 22 Oct 2012. A sibling petition filed today faces a wait of roughly 14 years.

facts.title: Border Patrol encounters of Peruvian nationals
facts.text: Border Patrol recorded 74,665 encounters of Peruvian nationals at the southwest border in FY2023, 33,974 in FY2024, 2,143 in FY2025 and 427 in FY2026. Totals are summed from CBP's public encounters file.

mechanics.asylumNote: 611 grants and 2,424 denials in immigration court, FY2024 (611 of 3,035 decisions, 20.1 percent); 1,562 more not adjudicated. EOIR Asylum Decisions by Nationality, https://www.justice.gov/eoir/media/1344846/dl
